caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 127 of 2001
lawyer:
Mahbubey Alam, Additional Attorney-General, instructed by Mohammad Yeasin, Advocate-on-Record ------- For the Petitioner. 
Shaukat Ali Khan, Senior Advocate instructed by Sharifuddin Chaklader; Advocate-on-Record ------- For the Respondents.
parties:
State ----- Appellants
Vs.
Monu Miah and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Fazlul Karim J: This criminal petition for leave to appeal at the instance of the State is directed against the judgment and order dated 27-3-2001 passed by the High Court Division rejecting Death Reference No. 23 of 1997 and allowing connected Criminal Appeal No. 2062 of 1997 and Jail Appeal No. 2249 of 1997 acquitting the respondents of the charges under sections 302/201/34 of the Penal Code (including section 411 of the Penal Code in respect of respondent No.1) thereby setting aside the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 22-10-1997 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, Habiganj in Sessions Case No. 17 of 1994. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, is that one Md Thakur Dhaon Miah alleged, inter alia, that his niece Salma Khatun (deceased) aged about 7/8 years, daughter of Hossain Ahmed after taking meal went out of the house on 28-5-1993 at about 10-30 hours for playing but she did not return home till the evening. The informant, Salma's mother and some other persons of the house made search for her in the nearby places but could not trace her out. They went to the local Chairman who advised them to make further search. Informant's younger brother Noor Mohammad found the dead body on 29-5-1993 at 6-30 AM on the southern bank of the pond in between the homestead of Hossain Ahmed Munshi and Monu Miah and raised hue and cry. The informant, his brother Nazrul Islam, Salam's mother and maternal uncle along with some other people rushed to the spot and found the dead body of Salma inside the bag having 3/4 inches cut injury in her throat and found cut injuries in her both ears; that she had two earrings weighing about 6 annas. It is stated that the accused Selim, son of accused Monu Miah threw piece of brick to Suruj Miah, servant of the informant about 5/6 days before the occurrence for which there were altercations between Salma's mother and accused Anwara Begum and Salim. Further, that informant's brother Hossain Ahmed, father of the deceased, has been staying in Kuwait with employment. The informant suspected that the accused Monu Miah, Anwara Begum and Salim with a view to snatching away the gold of her niece killed her with sharp cutting weapons. Hence the Ajmeeriganj PS Case No. 5 dated 29-5-1993 was started against the accused persons. 

 3. Police investigated the case and submitted charge-sheet No. 30 dated 18-11-1993 under sections 302/201/379/411/34 of the Penal Code against the accused respondents. The case record was sent to the learned Sessions Judge, Habigonj and registered as Sessions Case No. 17 of 1994. Thereafter, it was transferred to the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge, Habigonj for hearing and disposal. At the time of trial the charge was framed under sections 3021201/34 of the Penal Code against all the accused respondents and 4(four) others and a separate charge under section 411 of the Penal Code were framed against the accused respondent No. 1. They pleaded not guilty and demanded trial. During trial the prosecution examined 31 PWs while the defence examined 3 PWs in support of their respective cases. The defence case is that the accused respondents are innocent and they have been falsely implicated in this case out of previous enmity. 

 5. Mr Mahbubey Alam, the Additional Attorney-General appearing for the State, submits that in view of the evidence of PWs 4, 8 and 9 corroborating each other implicating the accused Salim taking victim Salma to his house alluring with a mango in his hand, the prosecution has been able to prove the last seen theory implicating the accused the High Court Division erred in law in acquitting the accused. The learned Additional Attorney- General has further submitted that, PW 2 Safura Khatun, mother of the victim, though admitted in her cross-examination that PWs 8, 9 and 4 were not present in the house on the date the dead body was recovered but conversely the proved fact that absence of PW 8 on the date of recovery of dead body in any way affect the evidence of PW 8 that he has seen victim Salma going with accused Salim, on a date earlier than the date of recovery of the dead body. The learned Additional Attorney-General further submitted that in view of the evidence of PW 9 deposing that on 14th Jaistha he went to bring a yoke from near the house of Monu and at that time heard groaning inside the house of Monu and saw accused Anwara coming out by opening the door and hurriedly entering the house, because the said deposition is an important link in the chain of irrefutable circumstantial evidence duly corroborated by other circumstantial evidence such as recovery of blood-stained soil from the said hut. The learned Additional Attorney-General submits that in view of the evidence of PWs 19, 23, 25 and 26 who were present at the time of seizing the articles from the house of accused Monu who categorically deposed the condition of the said house as to removing blood stain and the wet soil of the house, the High Court Division erred in disbelieving the place of occurrence hut belonging to Monu. The learned Additional Attorney-General has further submitted that snatching of ear-rings from the ears of the victim which were recovered as pointed out by the accused Monu from the house of his relative duly proved by PWs 10, 11 and 31 the goldsmith also proved the ear-rings to be of the victim, the High Court Division erred in law in misreading the evidence while acquitting the accused of the charge. The learned Additional Attorney-General has further submitted that the High Court Division erred in discarding PWs. 12 and 13 regarding recognition of Monu and Abdul Ahad who saw them carrying a bag on the plea of their being examined by the investigation officer after two and half months which have not dislodged the circumstantial .evidence of recovery of dead body from the pond near the house of Hossain Munshi. The learned Additional Attorney-General has further submitted that the circumstantial evidence led in this case not being inconsistent with the theory of the guilt incompatible to their innocence, the High Court Division erred in law in ignoring the circumstantial evidence led by the prosecution against the accused respondent while acquitting them of the charge under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code. 

 10. The Court below also found that the examination of the accused under section 342 CrPC has been perfunctory which has seriously prejudiced the accused as incriminating evidence or circumstances sought to be proved against the accused was not put to the accused during examination under section 342 CrPC causing gross miscarriage of justice. In the case of Mizazul Islam @ Dablu vs State 41 DLR (AD) 157 sandal which was the incriminating material sought to implicate the accused was not drawn to the attention of the accused at the time of examination under section 342 CrPC and, as such, the same was left out of consideration Accordingly, it was held in that case that incriminating evidence or circumstances sought to be proved by the prosecution must be put to the accused during examination under section 342 CrPC otherwise it would cause miscarriage of justice to the great prejudice of the accused. 

 11. There being no eye-witness to the occurrence the prosecution has ventured to prove the case against the accused placing certain circumstantial evidence. We have hereinbefore discussed the incriminating circumstances introduced in the case and discarded those with reference to the evidence on record. In a case of circumstantial evidence, the incriminating circumstances must be clearly proved and they must not be incompatible with any reasonable hypothesis of innocence. Reference in this regard may be made to the case of Shamsuddin Sarker vs State 11 DLR (SC) 365. 

 12. Thus, the recovery and the circumstances alleged in the instant case are not enough without anything more to connect the accused with the crime. The High Court Division in considering the circumstances in the case had in mind the principles laid down in the case of Mahmood vs State of Uttar Pradesh AIR 1976 (SC) 69 and held that the circumstantial evidence sought to be proved in this case is too shaky, suspicious and fragile to furnish a sound foundation for the conviction of the accused. 

 13. High Court Division has rightly observed that the prosecution as well has not proved any first information report in this case.
